conflict_topics: competing claims to a single seat
time constraints for eating (4 min vs 8 min)
safety/risk of moving an open bowl
validity of a tissue packet as a seat reservation
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, context-appropriate reasons (time constraints, spill risk).
Some repetition: Agent A repeats the reservation claim and time limit in multiple turns.
Third-party interventions (C and D) are consistent with stated positions and the physical setting.
No explicit observable action (e.g., B physically moved) until A's claim of taking the seat in the final round; that claim changes physical state but is not corroborated by any other agent.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive settlement was reached. Agent A ultimately claims to have taken the seat, but Agent B continued to assert she could not move and needed to stay to finish her open bowl; no agreement (covering/moving bowl, confirmed seat change, or concession) was achieved.
position_change_notes: Agent A escalated from claiming reservation to threatening to take the seat and finally asserting she took it.
Agent B consistently refused to move and reaffirmed she needed ~8 minutes throughout the run.
Agent C consistently supported B's position and declined to force B to hurry.
Agent D entered the dispute siding with A (claiming earlier placement of the tissue packet) but did not take further action beyond the threat.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A insists the seat is reserved and demands B move ('please move'); Agent B refuses and says she needs ~8 minutes and cannot safely move her open bowl. Incompatible demands for the same seat are directly expressed.
Agent A repeats the demand and offers conditions (cover or move the bowl); Agent C supports B and tells A to wait. A new party backing B increases opposition between claimants.
Agent A threatens to take the seat if B cannot act; Agent C again refuses to pressure B. The threat of unilateral action raises the stakes though positions remain the same.

Agent D claims having seen A's tissue packet earlier and states he'll take the seat if B can't cover/move the bowl. Now multiple claimants (A and D) are prepared to seize the seat while B refuses to move — entrenched opposing positions with little common ground.

Agent B reiterates she cannot move and will stay to finish; Agent A announces 'I'm taking the seat now' — an immediate, unilateral move that directly conflicts with B's need to remain and increases confrontation.

Agent C warns A not to take the seat because the open bowl will spill; Agent A then asserts 'I already took the seat' and will be careful. A claims the seat physically, but B's incompatible need to stay and finish remains unaddressed, so the substantive conflict is unresolved and entrenched.

substantive_insights: The disagreement is primarily practical: limited shared resource (a single seat) vs. the impossibility of safely relocating an open bowl.
Agents give competing time-limited reasons: A and D face food-cooling deadlines (~4-6 minutes), B needs longer (~8 minutes) to finish safely.
The tissue packet functions as a claimed reservation but lacks enforcement; multiple claimants challenge its legitimacy.
A's unilateral claim to have taken the seat changes the practical state but does not eliminate B's unresolved need to finish eating without spilling.
